title: Vessel - SPČR 2018 Exam Tests
description: Exam questions on vessel handling for divers (CMAS / SPČR (Czech Diving Federation))

questions.question: The transom of an inflatable boat is:

options.text: the bottom with smooth floorboards
the rigid vertical stern section used for mounting the outboard motor
the rear-view mirror at the bow of the boat
the front canopy of the boat

questions.explanation: The transom is the rigid stern section to which the outboard motor is mounted.

questions.question: When approaching a mooring buoy with a boat, the safest approach is:

options.text: downwind
with the current
into the current or wind
perpendicular to the current

questions.explanation: Heading into the current or wind gives better control over the boat and makes it easier to stop.

questions.question: On the skipper's command 'Drop anchor!', the designated crew member:

options.text: throws the prepared anchor as far as possible
drops the prepared anchor straight down immediately
lowers the anchor carefully only after spotting a shoal
none of the answers is correct

questions.explanation: The anchor is dropped straight down — never thrown, as that could damage the boat or injure crew.

questions.question: From the chart we have determined that we must steer a course over ground COG = 205°. To correct for magnetic variation, which we have set as +3°, and deviation, which is +2° for this heading, we will steer a compass course of:

options.text: compass course = 200°
compass course = 204°
compass course = 205°
compass course = 210°

questions.explanation: Compass course = COG − variation − deviation = 205° − 3° − 2° = 200°.

questions.question: A capsized inflatable boat:

options.text: we attempt to right, but we do not abandon it even if we fail
we attempt to right, and if we fail, we swim — even to a distant shore
we must absolutely manage to right
we do not attempt to right, so as not to exhaust ourselves

questions.explanation: Never abandon a capsized boat — it provides buoyancy and is more visible to rescuers.

questions.question: One knot (1 kn) is a unit of:

options.text: speed equal to 1 nautical mile per hour
distance equal to 1/10 of a nautical mile
speed equal to 1 km per hour
depth equal to 1.83 m

questions.explanation: A knot is a unit of speed equal to 1 nautical mile per hour (1.852 km/h).

questions.question: The entry '045' in the deck log means:

options.text: an easterly heading
a north-westerly heading
a north-easterly heading
a south-westerly heading

questions.explanation: 045° is a north-easterly heading (between north 0° and east 90°).

questions.question: Compared with displacement mode, navigating in planing mode results in:

options.text: higher speed and higher fuel consumption (per km)
higher speed and lower fuel consumption (per km)
lower speed and lower fuel consumption (per km)
lower speed and higher fuel consumption (per km)

questions.explanation: On the plane, speed is higher and fuel consumption per kilometre is lower thanks to reduced drag.

questions.question: A vessel must keep a lookout:

options.text: only in reduced visibility
by sight and hearing continuously
by hearing in fog and by sight at night
only when navigating in inshore waters

questions.explanation: A vessel must keep a continuous visual and aural lookout at all times.

questions.question: In 1998, the magnetic variation derived from a chart entry 'Var 2°W (1992) incr. 20' annually' will be:
questions.explanation: Over 6 years (1992–1998) the variation increased by 6 × 20' = 2°. The original 2°W + 2° = 4°W.

questions.question: On European coasts, tidal phenomena occur:

options.text: approximately twice in 25 h, both ebb and flood
once every 25 h (one flood every 12 h 25 min)
every 12 h 25 min — flood at spring tide and every 6 hours at neap tide
every 12 h 25 min — ebb at neap tide and every 6 hours at spring tide

questions.explanation: On European coasts there are roughly 2 high tides and 2 low tides in about 25 hours (one tidal day).

questions.question: After anchoring a larger boat in a current:

options.text: we anchor downstream
we let the propeller idle at low revs
we trail a floating line from the stern with a buoy or lifebuoy
we hoist the 'vessel in current' flag

questions.explanation: Trail a floating line with a buoy from the stern in case anyone falls overboard.

questions.question: The compass course allowing for current set is most easily determined:

options.text: graphically, from the speed and direction of the current alone
graphically, from the speed and direction of the current and the speed and course over ground (COG) of the vessel by vector subtraction
always by adding the magnitude of the current's speed to the vessel's speed
always by subtracting the magnitudes of the current's speed and the vessel's speed

questions.explanation: Compensating for current set is found graphically by vector subtraction of speeds and directions.

questions.question: Every vessel must proceed at a safe speed, meaning:

options.text: fast enough to overtake another vessel quickly
according to her length (e.g. a 7-metre boat at most 7 knots)
fast enough to alter her course immediately by 30°
such that she can avoid collision, including by stopping if necessary, in any conditions

questions.explanation: Safe speed is one that allows collision to be avoided in any conditions.

questions.question: The chain between the anchor line and the anchor:

options.text: increases the strength of the line
ensures the pull on the anchor stays as parallel to the seabed as possible and dampens shock loads on the cleat in waves
increases the weight of the anchor
is of no significance for anchoring

questions.explanation: The chain ensures a horizontal pull on the anchor and dampens shock loads caused by waves.

questions.question: When climbing out of the water onto a small inflatable boat after a dive, the first thing to do is:

options.text: place the mask in the boat
push the mask onto the forehead, but only remove it once on board
remove the fins
hand up the weights

questions.explanation: First hand up the weights, to make the climb easier and avoid loading the boat all at once.

questions.question: In 2000, the magnetic variation derived from a chart entry 'Var. 1°W (1994) decr. 30' annually' will be:
questions.explanation: Over 6 years (1994–2000) the variation decreased by 6 × 30' = 3°. The original 1°W − 3° = 2°E.

questions.question: When climbing aboard a boat by ladder after a dive:

options.text: we climb the ladder immediately, in close succession
we keep a careful watch on our surroundings, and in warm seas mainly look out for sharks
no one may stay directly beneath the ascending diver
all answers are correct

questions.explanation: No one may stay directly beneath the ascending diver because of the risk of dropped equipment or a fall.

questions.question: When two power-driven vessels approach one another:

options.text: each alters course to port
if they are head-on, each alters course to starboard
the vessel that has the other on her starboard side has right of way
the faster vessel has right of way

questions.explanation: In a head-on situation, both vessels alter course to starboard (port-to-port passing).

questions.question: Latitude is the coordinate of a point measured as an angle in the direction:

options.text: from the pole to the equator
from the equator to the pole
from the Greenwich meridian eastwards
from the Greenwich meridian westwards

questions.explanation: Latitude is measured from the equator towards the poles (0° to 90° N or S).

questions.question: In displacement mode, what has the greatest effect on navigation is:

options.text: the current
the wind
wind gusts
water temperature

questions.explanation: In displacement mode (low speed), the current has the greatest effect because it acts on the entire submerged hull.

questions.question: Navigation lights must be displayed:

options.text: only at night
whenever another vessel approaches
only when navigating in reduced visibility
from sunset to sunrise, in reduced visibility, and whenever deemed necessary

questions.explanation: Lights are displayed from sunset to sunrise, in reduced visibility, and whenever necessary.

questions.question: A cause of fuel starvation in the engine cannot be:

options.text: an empty fuel tank
a corroded contact on the ignition coil
a closed fuel-tank vent screw
a clogged fuel filter

questions.explanation: A corroded ignition-coil contact is an electrical-system fault, not a fuel-system fault.

questions.question: In 1999, the magnetic variation derived from a chart entry 'Var 1°W (1995) decr. 30' annually' will be:
questions.explanation: Over 4 years (1995–1999) the variation decreased by 4 × 30' = 2°. The original 1°W − 2° = 1°E.

questions.question: The main advantage of fixing one's position from bearings on 3 points using the inscribed-angle property of a circle is:

options.text: that we obtain a third intersection of position lines
that current set need not be considered
that only magnetic variation needs to be taken into account, not deviation
that it is not necessary to correct compass bearings to true bearings

questions.explanation: With the three-point method there is no need to correct compass bearings — only the angles between the points are used.

questions.question: The anchor line of an inflatable boat should be:

options.text: equal to the depth over which we intend to anchor
at least twice the depth over which we intend to anchor

questions.explanation: The anchor line should be at least twice the water depth so the anchor sets properly.

questions.question: We measure the distance between two points on a chart:

options.text: on the northern edge of the chart
on the southern edge of the chart, at approximately the same longitude
on the eastern or western edge of the chart, at approximately the same latitude
on the scale in the chart legend

questions.explanation: Distances are read off the side edge of the chart (latitude scale) at the corresponding height.

questions.question: An action taken to avoid collision shall be made:

options.text: by gradually altering the course
by gradually altering the speed
by altering course and speed in such a way that it is readily apparent to the other vessel
by altering course by less than 30°

questions.explanation: The change must be large enough to be readily apparent to the other vessel.

questions.question: A sheared shear-pin on the propeller will cause:

options.text: an increase in engine revs and the boat to slow down
a sudden increase in engine revs and the boat to accelerate
the boat to spin
the engine to stop

questions.explanation: Without the shear-pin the propeller spins freely — engine revs rise, but the boat slows down.

questions.question: After a group of divers has dived from the boat, the most important thing before leaving the site is:

options.text: to do a detailed debrief
to download dive profiles from the computers
to check that all dive participants are on board
to check that all divers have stowed their kit properly

questions.explanation: The most important thing is to confirm all divers are on board before departing.

questions.question: If the point on which we are taking a bearing lies to the south-west of us, the compass reading is:
questions.explanation: South-west is 225° (between south 180° and west 270°).

questions.question: To fix a position by terrestrial navigation (within sight of fixed landmarks), we need to know at least:

options.text: one position line
two position lines
three position lines
the speed of our boat

questions.explanation: An unambiguous fix requires at least two position lines (their intersection).

questions.question: When climbing out of the water onto a small inflatable boat after a dive:

options.text: first remove the fins and stow them in the boat together with the mask
lift the weights into the boat and either clip the scuba unit to the boat or hand it to the crew
with the crew's help, climb into the boat in full kit
watch the surroundings carefully and look out for sharks

questions.explanation: First remove the weights and the scuba unit, only then climb aboard.

questions.question: To plot a prescribed course over ground COG = 035° and an expected distance of 30 nautical miles from our position on the chart, we use a navigation triangle and dividers, with this angle:

options.text: measured on the triangle by aligning with the nearest meridian, and the distance read off on the eastern edge of the chart
measured on the triangle by aligning with the nearest meridian, and the distance read off on the southern edge of the chart
measured on the triangle by aligning with the nearest parallel of latitude, and the distance read off on the eastern edge of the chart
transferred from the compass rose on the chart, and the distance read off on the southern edge of the chart

questions.explanation: The angle is measured against the meridian and the distance read off on the side (eastern/western) edge of the chart.

questions.question: A coastal breeze typically blows:

options.text: both morning and evening, towards the sea
in the morning towards the sea, in the evening towards the shore
in the morning towards the shore, in the evening towards the sea
both morning and evening, towards the shore

questions.explanation: In the morning the breeze blows towards the shore (the sea is warmer); in the evening it blows out to sea (the land is warmer).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: an easterly wind blows from the east, an easterly current flows to the east
an easterly wind blows to the east, an easterly current flows to the east
an easterly wind blows from the east, an easterly current flows from the east
an easterly wind blows to the east, an easterly current flows from the east

questions.explanation: Wind is named after the direction it comes from. A current is named after the direction it flows towards.

questions.question: The starboard sidelight is:

options.text: green, visible from dead ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam
green, visible from the beam to 22.5° abaft the beam
red, visible from dead ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam
red, visible from the beam to 22.5° abaft the beam

questions.explanation: The starboard sidelight is green and shines from dead ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam (112.5°).

questions.question: When divers are picked up directly by the boat, they board the ladder:

options.text: on the windward side and when the ladder is at its lowest point
on the windward side and when the ladder is at its highest point
on the leeward side and when the ladder is at its lowest point
on the leeward side and when the ladder is at its highest point

questions.explanation: Board on the leeward side (calmer water) and when the ladder is at its lowest (easier to step on).

questions.question: The port sidelight is:

options.text: green, visible from dead ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam
green, visible from the beam to 22.5° abaft the beam
red, visible from dead ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam
red, visible from the beam to 22.5° abaft the beam

questions.explanation: The port sidelight is red and shines from dead ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam (112.5°).

questions.question: If we want to follow a charted course COG = 270° with a determined magnetic variation of −3° and current set of −2°, and deviation can be neglected, the compass course we steer is:

options.text: compass course = 265°
compass course = 270°
compass course = 273°
compass course = 275°

questions.explanation: Compass course = COG − variation − set = 270° − (−3°) − (−2°) = 270° + 3° + 2° = 275°.

questions.question: When leading a group on a drift dive, you should:

options.text: ensure the whole group stays together
monitor every member's gas consumption
use the compass to check direction of travel and watch the agreed dive time
all answers are correct

questions.explanation: A drift-dive leader must do all of the above.

questions.question: When two power-driven vessels approach one another:

options.text: each alters course to starboard
the vessel that has the other on her starboard side has right of way
the faster vessel has right of way
the vessel that has the other on her port side has right of way

questions.explanation: Right of way belongs to the vessel that has the other on her port side (the give-way vessel is the one with the other on her starboard).

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT apply to a 'man overboard' procedure on an inflatable boat in a tidal current and wind:

options.text: The boat's stern swings to the opposite side from the one the casualty fell off.
A person is designated to keep the casualty in sight at all times.
The approach is made by drifting downstream onto the casualty.
The approach is made into the wind.

questions.explanation: The approach is not made by drifting onto the casualty — that would be dangerous. The approach is controlled.

questions.question: The chart datum (CD) is defined as:

options.text: the lowest level below which the water surface only rarely falls at low tide
the highest level above which the water surface only rarely rises at high tide
the water level halfway between maximum high tide and maximum low tide
the average water level at high tide during spring tide

questions.explanation: Chart datum is the lowest tidal level — depths on a chart are measured from this reference.

questions.question: One nautical mile (1 nm) is defined as the distance corresponding to:

options.text: 1 angular minute along a terrestrial meridian
1 angular minute along a terrestrial parallel of latitude
1 degree along a terrestrial meridian
1 degree along a terrestrial parallel of latitude

questions.explanation: A nautical mile corresponds to 1 angular minute along a terrestrial meridian (approximately 1852 m).

questions.question: What should the first buddy pair do when diving from a small boat?

options.text: Set off towards the dive target and cooperate with each other.
Check their kit personally and with each other below the surface, then set off towards the dive target.
Check their kit personally and with each other below the surface, then wait for the other pairs at the anchor line.
Check their kit personally and with each other below the surface, then check (and if needed improve) the boat's anchoring.

questions.explanation: The first pair check their kit and inspect / improve the boat's anchoring for everyone's safety.

questions.question: When diving from a small boat in waves, the most suitable place to put on the scuba unit is:

options.text: in the water once the unit is floating beside the boat on a tether
at the bow
at the stern
in the middle of the boat

questions.explanation: In waves it is safest to don the scuba unit in the water, where conditions are more stable.

questions.question: Which of the following statements does NOT apply?

options.text: The anchor in the boat should lie under the anchor line.
It is advisable to attach a buoy to the end of the anchor line.
The anchor line is fastened to a fixed point on the boat.
The anchor in the boat should lie on top of the anchor line, or beside it.

questions.explanation: The anchor should lie under the line, not on top of it, so the line can pay out freely.

questions.question: To safely mark the position of a surfacing diver before pickup by the boat, the device used is:

options.text: rising bubbles
a delayed surface marker buoy (DSMB)
a pre-arranged acoustic signal
the 'distress on surface' signal

questions.explanation: A DSMB reliably marks the diver's position for pickup by the boat.

questions.question: Removing fins before climbing aboard a boat by ladder:

options.text: is necessary in all circumstances
is fundamentally inadmissible
is appropriate when using a conventional ladder
is appropriate when using a ladder with a centre rail

questions.explanation: On a conventional ladder it is appropriate to remove fins; on a ladder with a centre rail it is not necessary.
